planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or divisions in spring once frost has passed so the wiry, node-rooting stems can establish in cool, humid shade before summer dry spells.

directions: Luzuriaga polyphylla is a wiry-stemmed Chilean vine, closely related to Philesia and Lapageria, that either sprawls across the forest floor or climbs mossy tree trunks by rooting at its nodes. Its small, grey-green, scale-like leaves resemble a dwarf butcher's-broom, and in summer it produces solitary, fragrant, pendant white flowers followed by pale berries eaten by birds. In Chile its tough fibrous stems are traditionally harvested for basketry and broom-making on the island of Chiloe. It needs the same cool, constantly humid, humus-rich shade as its Valdivian rainforest companions and resents drying winds or full sun.

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in sheltered, part-shaded ground with acidic, moisture-retentive soil so roots establish before the first winter.

directions: 'Alf Robbins' is a white-flowered sport of the Chilean lantern tree, selected from seedlings raised from the 'Ada Hoffmann' clone and the first in the family to display pure white rather than the species' typical crimson-red hanging lantern blooms. It carries the same deeply incised, glossy evergreen leaves as the species but stays noticeably smaller and slower-growing, reaching only about 4 to 6 feet in height and spread, which suits it well to border or large-container culture. It shares the species' need for cool, humid, part-shaded sites with acidic, humus-rich, reliably moist soil, and benefits from winter protection against the hardest frosts in exposed gardens. It remains uncommon in cultivation and is propagated by cuttings taken from the named clone.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Best grown as a year-round terrarium or enclosed-case houseplant rather than an outdoor planting; divide offsets from an established rosette and pot into fresh humus-rich mix at any time indoors, timing outdoor moves (in zone 10-12 only) to after all danger of chill has passed.

directions: Grow in a sealed or high-humidity terrarium, vivarium, or glass case rather than open room air, since this low rosette-forming herb from the Atlantic rainforest floor of Bahia and Espirito Santo, Brazil wilts quickly once humidity drops below roughly 70 percent. Pot in a loose, humus-rich, well-drained mix and keep evenly moist but never waterlogged, since the fine hairy leaves rot readily if water sits on the foliage. Provide bright, indirect light only; direct sun scorches the velvety leaves, while too little light dulls the silvery-green central banding that gives the plant its jewel-like appeal. Divide clumps of rosettes to propagate, since this species is typically offered by specialist terrarium growers rather than mainstream nurseries.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens Kew — Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Grown year-round as an indoor terrarium or shaded-greenhouse foliage plant; separate rooted stolons or offsets from the parent clump and pot into fresh mix at any time indoors, or move container stock outdoors in zone 10-12 only once nights stay reliably warm.

directions: Pot in a loose, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic mix and keep consistently moist, since this stoloniferous forest-floor aroid from the humid lowland and lower-montane rainforests of Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, and Borneo comes from permanently damp leaf litter. Provide bright, indirect light and high humidity; low light is tolerated but dulls the silvery venation that traces the margins of the glossy, pointed leaves, while direct sun scorches the foliage. Spreading, creeping stolons readily root at the nodes, making division the simplest way to produce new plants for terrariums, vivaria, or shaded plantings. Keep off drafts below about 60 degrees F, since cold and dry air both cause rapid leaf decline in this specialist aroid-collector plant.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens Kew — Plants of the World Online
